strengths: Modeling modalities through coupled, potentially different latent variables is a useful perspective on multimodal representation learning.
The synthetic experiments examine several assumption violations and report results over three repetitions, providing useful empirical diagnostics.

The proposed CLIP post-processing is simple and evaluated across multiple encoders, distribution shifts, and 11 few-shot datasets. Reported improvements are promising; for example, the ViT16 two-shot target average increases from 32.51% to 37.13%.
weaknesses: The central identifiability proofs rely on an incorrect lemma. Appendix D.1, Lemma 5.1 claims that the normalized contrastive objective has global minimum zero. However, under the paper's uniform-sphere/vMF model with matched temperature, identity latent encoders attain -2I(z_x;z_t), which is negative for dependent modalities. Furthermore, condition C1 requires identical representations almost surely for positive pairs. With the full-support noisy conditional, this forces constant representations, contradicting the uniformity condition C2. Consequently, the argument establishing a shared encoder and elimination of modality-specific variables, used in both Theorems 4.1 and 4.3, is invalid.

The convex-body proof additionally substitutes an unjustified uniform marginal. A uniform p(z_x) and a normalized distance-based conditional on a bounded domain generally produce nonuniform p(z_t), because boundary effects make the conditional normalizer depend on z_x. Appendix E's Lemma 4.2 addresses only the limit as lambda approaches zero, but Eq. (43) uses exact uniformity at finite lambda. Corollary 4.4 also omits the appendix's essential restriction to Lp metrics with p different from 2; a general norm includes Euclidean geometry, which permits rotations rather than only scaled permutations.

The theoretical justification for FastICA does not follow. The uniform spherical prior has dependent Cartesian coordinates and is rotationally invariant, so it does not satisfy the independent-source assumptions needed to identify an ICA orientation. Having M-1 intrinsic dimensions does not resolve this incompatibility. The proposed local-isometry/PCA argument likewise does not establish that CLIP's spherical geometry satisfies the conditions required for permutation identifiability.

The downstream experiments do not isolate disentanglement as the source of improvement. FastICA includes centering, whitening, and dimension reduction, with different retained dimensions across configurations. Matched PCA-only and whitening-only baselines are missing. After fixed whitening, an orthogonal ICA rotation preserves dot products and the optimally solved L2-regularized linear-probe objective, making these controls particularly consequential.

The evidence does not establish the claimed real-world validation of identifiability. CelebA results consist of selected latent traversals without quantitative disentanglement measurements or matched PCA/random-direction controls; the 'gender with mustache' example itself changes multiple attributes. Downstream classification improvements cannot establish recovery of unknown ground-truth factors. Additionally, the synthetic R-squared evaluation predicts learned representations from true factors, which alone does not demonstrate invertible recovery.

The causal contribution and novelty are overstated. The undirected coupling specifies statistical dependence, but the paper does not formalize its intervention semantics or establish an identifiable causal query. The geometric recovery arguments substantially reuse Zimmermann et al. [67], while the proposed multimodal bridge has the correctness problems described above. A distinct advance beyond existing statistical multiview models or partially specified causal structures is therefore not established.

Reproducibility and uncertainty reporting are incomplete. The data used to fit PCA/ICA, whitening configuration, component-selection protocol, and several synthetic training details are insufficiently specified. Real-world results lack uncertainty estimates across few-shot sample selections. These omissions make it difficult to assess the reliability of smaller improvements or reproduce the preprocessing fairly.
